Cc: priya.singh@aurora-retail.com

Subject: Realtime inference errors: high-latency spikes today

Hi Grace / Marissa,

We experienced a repeated spike in tail latency across our production inference calls starting ~08:45 PST today and a corresponding jump in 5xx rates (from ~0.2% -> 4.3%) for the next 35 minutes. Throughput also dropped as traffic started timing out and client-side retries increased. Impact: 2 critical checkout flows slowed, a high-volume campaign saw ~18% drop in conversions during the window.

Attached is a small sample of request_ids and logs (aurora_logs_20261120.zip). Key request ids: req_9b31f, req_9b5a4, req_9c02d. We also saw a cluster of requests that fell back to the CPU path (X-Serving-Node: cpu-fallback). Can you confirm if anything changed on the Redwood side (deploy, quantization, config)? We need an interim summary + next steps and expected timelines for a full RCA.

Thanks,
Daniel
Sr. Platform Ops | Aurora Retail

Daniel — thanks for the signal and the logs. I'm taking point on coordination. Immediate notes:

- We see the same request_ids in our front-line logs and traced the CPU-fallback line you called out.
- No scheduled platform-wide deploys at 08:40; however, we rolled a model quantization config to the dedicated pool on 2026-11-19 02:30 UTC (small perf delta expected). Investigation is ongoing as to whether that triggered increased KV-cache churn for longer sequences.

What I'll deliver now: an "interim incident summary" with timeline + known impact within 4 hours, and a proposed remediation roster with owners and deadlines within 8 hours. We'll treat this as an executive-tier escalation until we have the RCA.

I've looped in Vivek (serving/runtime) and Karthik (customer reliability) to drive fixes and rollback options.

Next steps (short):
- Vivek to confirm immediate mitigation (increase pool headroom / explicit cache warming) — ETA 60–90 mins.
- Karthik to confirm whether we should roll back the quantization profile for Aurora's dedicated pool — ETA 3 hours.
- Marissa to coordinate credit/contract response and schedule a readout with Aurora execs — ETA 2 hours.

I'll send the interim summary as an attachment to this thread.

Best,
Grace O'Connor

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T10:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Realtime inference errors: high-latency spikes today

Summary of early findings (quick, non-final):

- Symptom: sustained tail latency > 700ms and ~3–5% 5xx rate between 08:45–09:20 PST; backlog spiked on pool-redwood-dedicated-aurora-1.
- Probable trigger: quantized kernel memory footprint + sequence-length distribution shift from recent campaign (avg seq len up ~2.9x for the window) -> higher KV eviction pressure and more frequent fallback to CPU serving path for some request slices.
- Contributing factor: autoscaler thresholds were tuned to prioritize latency SLOs but did not account for a sudden shift in sequence length distribution; the scaling decision was slightly delayed due to a recently tightened scale cooldown.

Immediate mitigations performed (10:15–10:40 PST):
- Increased reserved headroom on aurora-1 pool by +30% (manual) to absorb burst.
- Pinned KV cache reservations for heavy-prefetch entries for known campaign prefixes.
- Temporarily disabled the most aggressive quantization flag for the aurora pool (rolling revert started at 10:22 UTC).

Next actions (owners / ETA):
- Full rollback of quantization for aurora pool (owner: karthik_iyer) — ETA 3 hours, will monitor for regression.
- Autoscaler tune: reduce cooldown and add sequence-length metric to scale decision (owner: vivek_kulkarni) — ETA 48 hours for safe rollout.
- Postmortem: full RCA with timeline, root cause, and actionable long-term mitigations (owner: vivek_kulkarni) — ETA 72 hours.

I'll feed a short status update back into this thread after the rollback completes.

-- Vivek
VP, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
